newsitem.title: EGYPT: EU Middle East envoy sees danger to peace process.
newsitem.headline: EU Middle East envoy sees danger to peace process.

text.p: The European Union's envoy to the Middle East said on Saturday the peace process was in danger and he would urge Russia to play a more active role in salvaging deadlocked talks between Israel and the Palestinians.
Miguel Angel Moratinos told reporters in Cairo that senior EU officials might hold a meeting next week to examine ways the 15-member bloc could revive the talks.

"The situation has become very dangerous," he said after talks with Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa. "The peace process must be saved. The European Union will do all it can through diplomatic channels to save the peace process."

Moratinos said he would head for Gaza on Sunday for talks with Palestinians and then to Israel. He would then go to Russia, which along with the United States is a sponsor of the Middle East peace effort launched in Madrid in 1991.
His visit to Russia would aim to "boost the Russian role at this difficult time", Moratinos said. "We are very worried about the present situation. We must do all we can to overcome this crisis."
Talks between Israel and the Palestinians have been on hold since the Jewish state broke ground on a settlement in East Jerusalem in March.

Moussa, who earlier met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani, told reporters the only way to rescue the peace process was to persuade Israel to stop building settlements on occupied land.

"The peace process cannot be salvaged unless the reasons that led to its deterioration are treated. The main reason is settlements, especially what happened in Jerusalem and occupied Palestinian land. Also, (Israel's) lack of seriousness in its redeployment," Moussa said.

"Israel's obstinacy is the reason for this deterioration because its repeated statements that it will not stop settlements has caused and continues to cause the breakdown in the peace process," he added.
Moussa urged the United States to make the most of its influence to forge a breakthrough in the stalled talks.

"Negotiations have been frozen because of the Israeli stance. The U.S. Secretary of State (Madeleine Albright), due to her experience and position, enjoys a lot of influence which can benefit these difficult circumstances in which the doors of peace are being closed one after the other because of Israel's obstinacy," Moussa said.

Albright said at a meeting with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy on Friday that she was not prepared to visit the region until the parties made the "difficult decisions" required to break the current deadlock.
She said that the U.S. could provide only limited help to move the Middle East peace process forward, and it was up to the Israelis and Palestinians to make the compromises needed.
